population.note: FICTIONAL. ~265M US adults × 18.3% ≈ 48.5M current users. Age check: 0.20×10 + 0.33×18 + 0.24×29 + 0.23×15 ≈ 18.4. Income check: (21+20+14)/3 ≈ 18.3. The bottom third gained the most in relative terms (cheap authorized generic, Medicaid opt-ins), but it still trails because of Medicaid work-requirement churn from Jan 2027, prior-auth paperwork and pharmacy access, not because of price. Cycling arithmetic: ever 25 = current 18.3 + off 6.7; current = 11.3 never-stopped (many of them 2027–28 starters) + 7.0 restarters; off = 4.7 stopped and never restarted + 2.0 restarted and stopped again; stopped-and-restarted = 7.0 + 2.0 = 9.0 → 9.0/25 = 36% of ever-users. That puts cumulative restart among stoppers at 9.0/13.7 ≈ 66%, above the 36–47% one-year figure from 2026. This is cumulative over 2–3 years, and the $49–69 generic removed the most common reason for stopping, which was cost or losing coverage. Off-drug populations: ~17.8M adults who used and are off now; ~2.4M of the 48.5M on drug report scheduled 'drug holidays' in a given quarter and are counted as current. Pediatric: ~0.5% of ~73M under-18s ≈ 365k, about 2.5% of children with obesity, up from ~0.6%. Most are aged 12–17. Medicaid/CHIP now pays for roughly half of them, which narrows the 2026 upper-income skew without removing it.

access.public_coverage: Medicare is now the largest single payer. CMS extended the GLP-1 Bridge demonstration past its Dec 2027 end through 2030 under existing CMMI authority, with the same BMI/comorbidity criteria and a $50 beneficiary copay. The IRA negotiated price for semaglutide took effect Jan 2027. 33 states plus DC opted their Medicaid programmes in at the federal reference rates. Payer mix of ~48.5M users: Medicare ~10.5M (21%), Medicaid ~6.5M (13%), VA/TRICARE/other federal ~1.5M (3%), so public ~18.5M (38%); cash ~18M (37%); employer ~12M (25%).
access.generic_rest_of_world: Generic semaglutide is routine in India ($8–40/month), China (patent lapsed 2026; dozens of domestic makers), Canada (~CAD 60–100), Brazil, Mexico and most of ~160 markets. Generic oral semaglutide is spreading abroad. Tirzepatide remains patented almost everywhere.
access.note: Authorized generic semaglutide injection (made by Novo and distributed under the Jan 2028 Paragraph IV settlement with Viatris) launched Jun 2028 at $49–69/month cash through pharmacy chains and cost-plus channels. Brand Wegovy/Ozempic list prices are nominally unchanged, but almost nobody pays them. Zepbound has no generic; cash vials run $299–449 and TrumpRx brand pricing is ~$245. Lilly cut Foundayo starting doses to $99 in response. Employer coverage fell to 52%. Many employers that kept coverage moved to generic-only tiers with step therapy before tirzepatide. Medicare spending arithmetic (annualised run-rate, end-2028): blended Medicare payment = 0.4 generic share × $79 + 0.6 brand × $245 ≈ $179/month; 10.5M × $179 × 12 ≈ $22.6B/yr. Medicaid: 6.5M × ~$140 blended × 12 ≈ $10.9B/yr gross, ~$7.1B federal at ~65% FMAP. Public gross run-rate ≈ $33.5B/yr, roughly the whole of CBO's ≥$35B nine-year score for the original pilot. Some Medicare beneficiaries now pay $49 cash for the generic rather than a $50 copay. Compounders have lost most of their price rationale. The residual gray market is personal importation of Indian and Chinese product and tirzepatide 'research peptides'.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic, plus US authorized generic from Jun 2028)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema, approved Mar 2027)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, approved Apr 2028, BMI≥35 or ≥30 with comorbidity)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda and generics)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: alcohol reduction: widely prescribed off-label with the generic; still no approval; phase 3 AUD trials ongoing
'drug holiday' and low-dose maintenance regimens for appetite and reward management
microdosing for 'metabolic health' by people without obesity, now cheap enough to be casual
nicotine and compulsive-behaviour reduction: observational evidence only
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
drugs.pipeline_note: Approvals in window: CagriSema (Mar 2027, under review at start of the window) and retatrutide (Apr 2028, ~13 months after its Q1 2027 BLA; labelled for dysesthesia; restricted to higher BMI). The muscle-preserving-combo driver is realised in the forms the rules allow. First, Novo launched CagriSema as a 'lean-sparing' combination on the strength of a DEXA substudy, a claim discredited in Oct 2027. Second, Lilly's bimagrumab + tirzepatide reported phase 3 body-composition data in mid-2028 (lean mass ~10% of weight lost vs ~25–30% on tirzepatide alone) and the BLA was filed Nov 2028 under a National Priority Voucher; a decision is expected 2029, so it is not on the market. Telehealth 'lean protocols' (drug + protein + resistance coaching) are sold as though the problem is already solved. Amycretin (phase 3), survodutide, MariTide (monthly) and amylin monotherapies are not on the US market. No new indications were granted in the window.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Most common class effect. Concentrated at initiation and escalation, and now also at each restart after a drug holiday, which re-exposes users to escalation-phase GI effects.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled. Restart-titration guidance added to prescribing information in 2027.

safety_ledger.effect: Severe or persistent gastroparesis, ileus and intestinal obstruction
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Delayed gastric emptying is pharmacologically established. Whether it causes severe gastroparesis that persists after stopping is contested. MDL 3094 (E.D. Pa.) passed 20,000 filed cases in 2028.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Ileus already labelled. Unsealed documents prompted an FDA labelling review; no new boxed warning. First bellwether trials are set for 2029.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A 2027 pooled analysis of CV-outcome trials again found no causal excess; absolute risk is low. Claims are now folded into the mass tort.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled. Litigation is at mass-tort scale alongside the gastroparesis claims.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Retained gastric contents at endoscopy and surgery. Volume rose with users; pre-procedure dose holds are routine.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; anaesthesia society guidance on peri-procedural holds.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss, notably with retatrutide.

~25–30% of weight lost is lean mass on mono- and dual agonists. Medicare enrolment of ~10.5M older adults has moved the concern into geriatrics and falls clinics. Novo's CagriSema 'lean-sparing' claim rested on a post-hoc subgroup; the prespecified analysis was null.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA untitled letter to Novo over CagriSema body-composition promotion (late 2027). Bimagrumab combination under review.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohort studies still conflict. Claims are consolidated separately from the GI litigation.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label; no US class label.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Now quantified in surveys: about 1 in 5 long-term users report reduced enjoyment beyond food, and most of them report improvement after a dose reduction or holiday. No RCT has been designed to measure it; observational instruments are being validated.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None on label. Professional societies published dose-reduction guidance, and manufacturers fund 'wellbeing' registries.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The conflict between trial and real-world figures persists. Weight cycling through holidays and Medicaid churn is now common.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None. Supports chronic-therapy framing by payers.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Concern is growing among older Medicare users and adolescents.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None; dietitian referral encouraged in Bridge criteria.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; adolescent decades-long use; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ~6 years of RCT follow-up. Cycling is now the majority real-world pattern and has never been the subject of a trial.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements on new approvals; no cycling study mandated.

safety_ledger.effect: Dysesthesia (skin sensitivity, abnormal sensation) with triple agonist
Compounded / counterfeit product harms (dosing errors, contamination)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: US compounding has shrunk sharply since generics, but harms from imported and 'research peptide' product persist, mostly tirzepatide.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 503B exclusion finalised; import alerts on peptide shipments.

food_and_beverage.state: GLP-1 households are ~31% of US households. Snack, confectionery and sugary-drink volumes are down low-to-mid single digits per year, and pricing and premiumisation offset some of the loss. 'GLP-1 companion' ranges are standard at large CPG firms. A small 'unmedicated indulgence' marketing niche is growing alongside the backlash.

alcohol.state: US spirits and beer volumes fell for a third year. Off-label alcohol prescribing of the cheap generic hit heavy drinkers, who account for most volume. Brands are pushing low/no-alcohol and 'occasion' positioning; distilleries and some brewers are consolidating.

restaurants.state: Traffic is roughly flat. Smaller plates, shareables and protein-forward menus are the norm. Spending per visit holds through premiumisation, but alcohol attach rates keep falling.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep contracting, slowed slightly by backlash-aligned 'unbothered' lines. Mainstream retailers carry a wider middle size range to serve people regaining weight.

fitness.state: Strength training and the 'muscle insurance' pitch drive growth. Gyms partner with telehealth on lean protocols, and Medicare Advantage plans add resistance-training benefits.

insurance.state: The cost has shifted to the public payer. Employers retreated to 52% coverage, mostly generic-only. Pharmacy trend moderated after the generic launch. Medicare and Medicaid now carry the volume, at a run-rate ~$33.5B/yr that far exceeds the original score.

pharma.state: Lilly leads on tirzepatide, Foundayo and retatrutide. Novo lost roughly a third of its market value after the unsealed documents and is defending volume with its own authorized generic. US net price per script is falling fast while volume rises. Litigation reserves are now a line item.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Thinness signals nothing at $49 a month. A visibly larger body now reads to some as a choice and a statement, and to others as a sign of poverty or a lapse in Medicaid paperwork.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Access is no longer a question of price but of floor conditions: a working pharmacy, stable Medicaid enrolment, an hour for a prior-auth call. The affluent differentiate on next-gen drugs (retatrutide, lean protocols, waiting for bimagrumab) and on muscle, not on thinness.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Family meals are commonly split between on-drug and off-drug eaters. Hosts plan 'holiday weekends' when guests skip doses for weddings and Thanksgiving. In Atlanta the church-hosted 'Whole Plate' suppers of the backlash movement treat a shared full meal as a ritual of refusal.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Dating profiles routinely state 'on / off / holiday'. Couples coordinate dose skips around anniversaries and trips. Reduced desire is a recognised complaint rather than a whisper.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: A visible counter-movement led by millennial women off the drug, MAHA-adjacent 'natural metabolic' influencers (berberine and fasting) and some Black and evangelical churches frames appetite as part of the self, and suppression as something done to people. Fat-acceptance language has revived on social platforms under the tag #Unsuppressed.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: Survey estimates put persistent reduced enjoyment at ~20% of long-term users. ~5% of current users (~2.4M) take a scheduled drug holiday in any given quarter, and low-dose 'maintenance' regimens are a standard clinic offer.
interior_life.framing: A side effect that is managed like a dial. Clinicians talk about 'titrating to life'. The same blunting is the reason off-label alcohol prescribing is spreading, so people describe it as a trade-off rather than a bug.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Managers in sales and hospitality joke about 'flat' teams. Some workers time holidays around launches or quarter-ends to get their edge back. Others say quieted craving improves focus. Employers do not ask and do not track.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Musicians and comedians talk openly about writing 'off-dose'. Live-music bar revenue is down with drinking. Extreme-flavour foods and high-intensity experiences (sour candy, spicy challenges, loud immersive venues) are marketed to people who want to feel something.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Reduced libido and connection are discussed in couples therapy as routine. Weekend dose skips for intimacy are common enough that clinicians warn about GI rebound on restart.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The backlash has a political voice without policy. Wellness-right and anti-pharma left influencers share the 'they want you numb' frame, and MAHA rhetoric attacks the drugs while the administration's coverage deals remain in force. No measurable effect on turnout.

state.regulatory_posture: Unchanged posture: still pro-access and pro-speed. There was no new legislation, mandate or conditioning in the window. Public expansion came from extending the existing CMMI demonstration, the IRA price taking effect as scheduled, and state Medicaid opt-ins. FDA's actions were routine: approvals, an untitled letter to Novo, and a labelling review.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate. Public coverage at negotiated rates with a $50 Medicare copay; Medicaid coverage in 33 states plus DC.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Only the BMI/comorbidity criteria and prior authorisation. Medicaid work requirements, enacted earlier and not aimed at these drugs, interrupt therapy through enrolment churn.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The US authorized generic is made by Novo, so there is no new API dependence. The US–India price gap has narrowed from ~40× to ~2–5×. Personal imports from Indian and Chinese makers persist for tirzepatide analogues.

events.event: Medicare's negotiated price for semaglutide takes effect; CMS announces that the GLP-1 Bridge demonstration will continue through 2030 at the same $50 copay; by year-end 33 state Medicaid programmes plus DC have opted in at the federal reference rates
FDA approves Novo Nordisk's CagriSema; Novo launches it as the first 'lean-sparing' weight-loss combination, citing a DEXA body-composition substudy

Documents unsealed in GLP-1 MDL 3094 show that Novo's prespecified CagriSema lean-mass analysis was null, that its marketing relied on a post-hoc subgroup, and that internal memos from 2018–19 minimised gastroparesis signals; Novo shares fall ~30%; FDA issues an untitled letter
Filed cases in the GLP-1 gastroparesis, ileus and pancreatitis MDL pass 20,000; the court schedules the first bellwether trials for 2029; law-firm ads run nightly on cable
Under a January Paragraph IV settlement with Viatris, Novo launches an authorized generic semaglutide injection at $49–69/month cash at major pharmacy chains, the first sub-$75 US incretin
The #Unsuppressed movement's 'Whole Plate' supper in Atlanta draws ~15,000 people across 40 churches and halls; Torrid sponsors and expands its 'Unbothered' line

open_tensions: Public payers now carry ~38% of users at a ~$33.5B/yr gross run-rate against a CBO score written for a pilot. As generic share rises, the cost falls, but the Medicare population keeps growing, and nobody has decided whether the demonstration becomes permanent law.
The 2029 bellwethers will test causation for persistent gastroparesis using Novo's unsealed documents. A settlement figure could reshape Novo's generic strategy and the labels of the whole class.
'Skinny-frail' is being sold as solved before the bimagrumab combination is approved, while ~10.5M older Medicare users lose lean mass on drugs with no muscle protection.

Cycling is now the majority pattern, driven by drug holidays for anhedonia, Medicaid churn and $49 casual restarts. It is the least studied way to take these drugs, and the ~365k children on them will cycle for decades.
still_true: Wegovy's list price is nominally $1,349 a month and almost nobody pays it
Medicare beneficiaries pay a ~$50 copay for covered obesity GLP-1s under the Bridge terms
No GLP-1 is FDA-approved for alcohol use disorder; alcohol reduction remains off-label
Foundayo (orforglipron) is on the market as Lilly's daily small-molecule oral
The FDA's January 2026 removal of the suicidal-ideation warning from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels stands

prose.headline: The $49 Shot: Cheap Semaglutide, 20,000 Lawsuits, and the Americans Who Want Their Hunger Back
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2028 nearly one American adult in five takes an incretin drug, and a quarter have taken one at some point. The number that changed this most was the price. In June, under a patent settlement Novo Nordisk signed with Viatris in January, an authorized generic semaglutide injection reached pharmacy counters at $49 to $69 a month. It is made by Novo itself. That is less than many people spend on streaming. The brand list prices still exist on paper, and nobody pays them.

The price fell after the payer had already changed. Medicare's obesity pilot was due to end in December 2027. Instead CMS quietly extended it to 2030. Thirty-three states and the District opted their Medicaid programmes in. No new law was passed, no mandate issued, and no one is monitored. A demonstration simply kept running until it became the default. Medicare is now the largest single payer, covering about ten and a half million people at a blended rate that falls each month as generic fills replace brand. The arithmetic gives about $22 billion a year for Medicare and $11 billion for Medicaid, roughly the whole of the nine-year budget score for the original pilot, now spent each year. Employers have kept retreating. About half still cover weight loss, and most of them will pay only for the generic.

For the poorest third of adults, price is no longer the barrier. Paperwork is. Medicaid work requirements that took effect in 2027 knock people off coverage for a month or two at a time, and each lapse means stopping, regaining weight, restarting and enduring the nausea again. Cycling is no longer an exception. More than a third of everyone who has ever used these drugs has stopped and started again.

Some cycling is chosen. The flattening people called 'Ozempic personality' in 2026 is now an ordinary complaint, raised in couples therapy, joked about in sales meetings and handled like a thermostat. Clinicians offer low 'maintenance' doses. People skip a week before a wedding, a tour or an anniversary, to taste the cake and to want each other again. Surveys put persistent loss of enjoyment at about one long-term user in five. Meanwhile doctors prescribe the cheap generic off-label to heavy drinkers precisely because it blunts reward. Brewers and distillers feel that more than anyone. They are in their third year of falling volume.

The drugs got stronger as they got cheaper. Lilly's retatrutide was approved in April with about 28 percent weight loss and a new labelled side effect, an abnormal sensitivity of the skin. Novo's CagriSema arrived in 2027 marketed as 'lean-sparing'. That claim fell apart in October 2027, when documents unsealed in the federal gastroparesis litigation showed the prespecified muscle analysis had found nothing, along with older internal memos playing down stomach-paralysis reports. Novo lost about a third of its value. The litigation, which now covers gastroparesis, bowel obstruction and pancreatitis, passed twenty thousand cases in February, and the first trials are set for 2029. Lilly's genuinely muscle-sparing combination with bimagrumab was filed in November and is not yet approved. Telehealth companies already sell 'lean protocols' as if it were.

The backlash has a body and an address. In Atlanta, under the #Unsuppressed banner, church suppers called Whole Plate draw thousands of women who have stopped the drug, along with their families and pastors, to eat full meals in public. Online, wellness influencers selling berberine and fasting share the slogan 'they want you numb' with anti-pharma voices on the left. Torrid sells a line for them. No policy has followed. A thin body now signals nothing, and at $49 a month it no longer marks wealth or effort.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Tammy Rourke wakes at five in Dayton and counts on her fingers. Sunday was her shot day, and she skipped it. Kaylee turns seven on Saturday, and Tammy wants to taste the cake.

At her first client's house, Mr. Abernathy is on the Medicare one, the fifty-dollar copay one. His thighs have gone soft as bread dough, and she helps him up from the recliner with both arms. His son has printed out a gym flyer that says MUSCLE INSURANCE.

At lunch in the car she eats half a turkey wrap and, for the first time in months, wants the other half. She eats it.

Her Medicaid lapsed in March over an hours form she had sent twice. The Kroger pharmacist rings up the generic at fifty-nine dollars and says, 'Same stuff, honey.' Tammy pays cash and doesn't bother with the appeal.

At four the radio plays a law-firm ad: Were you hospitalized with stomach paralysis? Then a song she used to love comes on, and this time it does something to her chest. She turns it up.

Her sister Dawn texts a photo of a church fellowship hall full of long tables: Whole Plate Sat. Bring Kaylee. You don't need that stuff.

Tammy types I'm off it this week, deletes it, and types Maybe.

At home she puts the pen in the butter compartment next to last week's. Her husband is watching the game with a beer he isn't drinking. He looks over and says she seems more like herself. She doesn't know if he means it kindly, or which self he means.
